# Maxine Zhou — Portfolio

A dependency-free static portfolio site, rebuilt from the original Wix site
(`maxinezhou03024.wixsite.com/mysite`) after the custom domain was disconnected.

**No build tools, no npm, no framework.** Plain HTML + one CSS file, generated by a
single Python script that ships with macOS.

---

## Quick start

Preview locally:

```bash
cd portfolio && python3 -m http.server 8787
```

Then open <http://localhost:8787>.

Regenerate the HTML after editing content:

```bash
cd portfolio && python3 build.py
```

That's it. No install step.

---

## How it fits together

```
portfolio/
├── build.py              ← ALL text content + page structure lives here
├── _dims.json            ← cached image dimensions (prevents layout shift)
│
├── index.html            ← generated — do not hand-edit
├── projects.html         ← generated
├── about.html            ← generated
├── 404.html              ← generated
├── work/*.html           ← generated (8 case studies)
│
├── assets/
│   ├── css/site.css      ← ALL styling. Design tokens at the top.
│   ├── img/              ← 108 images, resized to max 2000px
│   ├── video/            ← 7 product demo clips
│   ├── doc/              ← résumé PDF
│   └── favicon.svg
│
└── _reference/           ← scraped source material (not part of the site)
```

**The HTML files are generated output.** Edit `build.py` and re-run it — otherwise your
changes get overwritten on the next build.

### Two places to make changes

| I want to change… | Edit this |
|---|---|
| Wording, headings, project order, adding/removing a case study | `build.py` (the `CONTENT` section) |
| Colours, type, spacing, layout, component look | `assets/css/site.css` |

The two are deliberately decoupled: `build.py` emits semantic HTML with stable class
names, and `site.css` decides what it looks like. **A full visual redesign should not
require touching `build.py` at all.**

## Design tokens

These were extracted from the original Wix theme's compiled CSS, so the current look
matches the old site closely. All defined at the top of `site.css`:

| Token | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `--cream` | `#F4F0EB` | page background |
| `--cream-2` | `#FFF8F1` | warm card tint |
| `--ink` | `#191818` | primary text |
| `--ink-2` | `#504E4D` | secondary text |
| `--muted` | `#878482` | tertiary text, captions |
| `--brown` | `#5B4D43` | warm accent, eyebrows |
| `--tan` | `#E0BE9A` | accent, list markers, primary button |
| `--lav` | `#AFACFB` | accent (question cards) |
| `--line` | `#BDBAB6` | hairlines |

Type: **Instrument Sans** (headings/UI) + **Almarai** (body), both from Google Fonts —
these are the same two families the Wix site used.

## Saving to GitHub (private repo)

This folder is already a git repo with one commit. To get it onto GitHub without the
terminal:

1. Install **GitHub Desktop**: <https://desktop.github.com>
2. Sign in to your GitHub account when prompted.
3. `File → Add Local Repository…` → choose this `portfolio` folder. It will recognise the
   existing repo and commit.
4. Click **Publish repository**. **Leave "Keep this code private" ticked.**

After that, any future changes show up in GitHub Desktop as a diff — write a short summary,
click Commit, then Push.

## Deploying

The folder is a plain static site, so any static host works.

**Netlify is the right choice here**, because it deploys from **private** repos on the free
tier and supports custom domains.

- *Fastest, no git at all:* drag the `portfolio` folder onto <https://app.netlify.com/drop>.
  You get a live URL immediately. Attach your domain under Site settings → Domain management.
- *Better long-term:* in Netlify, "Add new site → Import an existing project" → connect
  GitHub → pick this repo. Leave the build command empty and set the publish directory to
  `/`. Every push then redeploys automatically.

**A note on GitHub Pages:** it only serves **public** repositories on the free GitHub plan —
publishing Pages from a private repo requires GitHub Pro. Since this repo is private
(it contains client Slack screenshots and internal product UI), use Netlify rather than
Pages, or accept making the repo public.

Once you have a real URL, set `BASE_URL` near the top of `build.py` and re-run it —
that switches on canonical tags, Open Graph/social preview tags, `sitemap.xml`, and
`robots.txt`. Leave it blank and those are simply omitted (harmless, just no rich
link previews when you paste the URL into LinkedIn or an email).

## Assets

- Images were downloaded at full resolution (202 MB), then resized to max 2000px wide
  and converted PNG→JPEG where there was no transparency. Result: **25 MB**.
- **Untouched full-resolution originals are at `../original-assets/`** (195 MB), outside
  this folder so they aren't deployed or committed. Don't delete them — they're the only
  copy if Wix takes the site down.
- Videos were pulled at 720p (the highest reliably available from Wix's CDN).

See `HANDOFF.md` for open questions, known gaps, and restyle notes.
